body.title: Introduce 'possibleSmartCasts' in 'KaScopeContext'
body.body: The new endpoint makes it possible to track potential smart casts in a particular position, even if a real cast isn't yet present in the source code.

      * The list is sorted according to the order of scopes in the scope tower (from innermost to outermost).
      */
     public val scopes: List<KaScopeWithKind>

+    /**
+     * The list of smart casts available at the context position.

+     * Note that the actual smart cast will only appear if the original expression type does not match the expected type.

+/**
+ * Represents a possible smart cast at a fixed context position.
+ *
+ * The word "possible" means that the compiler is allowed to produce smart casts for the [source] expression if there is a need to do so.
+ * Note that unless [isStable] is set, the smart cast will not be applied. In addition, the `SMARTCAST_IMPOSSIBLE` error is issued
+ * in certain cases.
+ */
+@KaExperimentalApi
+public interface KaSmartCastPossibility : KaLifetimeOwner {
+    /**
+     * A declaration, references to which smart cast may be applied (if [isStable] is `true`).
+     */
+    public val source: KaSmartCastSource<KaVariableSymbol>
+
+    /**
+     * Types that [source] may be automatically cast to.
+     */
+    public val resultingTypes: List<KaType>
+
+    /**
+     * Whether the smart cast [source] is stable at the context position.
+     *
+     * The same [source] can have different smart cast stability depending on the context position.
+     * Such as, in the code snippet below, a smart cast will be applied to the first usage of `value`. However, after the conditional
+     * expression, the compiler is not sure anymore that the `value` is still set, so a compilation error is reported.
+     *
+     * ```
+     * fun test() {
+     *     var value: String? = System.getProperty("some.property")
+     *     if (value == null) {
+     *         return
+     *     }
+     *
+     *     value.length  // Smart cast is applied
+     *
+     *     if (Random.nextBoolean()) {
+     *         value = null
+     *     }
+     *
+     *     value.length  // UNSAFE_CALL
+     * }
+     * ```

+     * For more information on the smart cast stability, check the Kotlin specification:
+     * [Smart cast sink stability](https://kotlinlang.org/spec/type-inference.html#smart-cast-sink-stability).
+     */
+    public val isStable: Boolean
+}

body.body: In the [specification](https://kotlinlang.org/spec/type-inference.html#smart-cast-sink-stability) "smart cast source" has a different meaning. In the spec terms, this is a smart cast sink. To avoid using the word "sink", maybe we should call it `KaSmartCastPosition`?

body.body:
Analysis from Codex:

Found three issues:

1. **[P1] New API is added to the frozen legacy surface** — [KaScopeProvider.kt:317](/Users/alexey.belkov/code/kotlin/analysis/analysis-api/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/analysis/api/components/KaScopeProvider.kt:317)

   `possibleSmartCasts` and its public types are under `components/`, which is frozen during the endpoint-architecture migration. `AnalysisApiLegacySurfaceDumpTest` and `AnalysisApiLegacyCallableDumpTest` both fail. This should be exposed from a domain package as a context-session endpoint rather than updating the legacy dumps.

2. **[P1] New public interfaces are unintentionally extensible** — [KaScopeProvider.kt:328](/Users/alexey.belkov/code/kotlin/analysis/analysis-api/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/analysis/api/components/KaScopeProvider.kt:328), [KaScopeProvider.kt:373](/Users/alexey.belkov/code/kotlin/analysis/analysis-api/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/analysis/api/components/KaScopeProvider.kt:373)

   `KaSmartCastPossibility` and `KaSmartCastSource` lack `@SubclassOptInRequired(KaImplementationDetail::class)` or `@KaSpi`. `AnalysisApiExtensibilityTest` consequently fails, and the current API accidentally promises client implementability.

3. **[P2] Dispatch-receiver smart casts are silently discarded** — [KaFirScopeProvider.kt:380](/Users/alexey.belkov/code/kotlin/analysis/analysis-api-fir/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/analysis/api/fir/components/KaFirScopeProvider.kt:380)

   FIR represents a member function’s `this` as a `FirRegularClassSymbol`, which becomes a class symbol rather than `KaVariableSymbol`. The `takeIf` therefore drops valid cases such as `if (this is Bar)`. Widen the source representation to `KaDeclarationSymbol` or explicitly model `this`, and add the existing LL `dispatchReceiver.kt` scenario to the Analysis API tests.
